title: One chassis, eight robots: I added a rover family to my post-apocalyptic game
author: DarthOrganism
selftext:
*(The video is slightly sped up)*

A short update on The Last Sand, the post-apocalyptic game I’m building with AI agents (Opus 5.5, Codex, Blender via MCP, Godot).

I added a family of enemy rovers. They all share one chassis, the combat rover from earlier parts, and differ only in the module on the roof. The variants live in one shared catalog, and each module has its own behavior. Models are 110–200 KB each, with no textures and one shared worn-paint material.

The lineup:

* **Gun**: machine gun, the base unit.
* **Beacon**: only comes out at night and fires a flare. Inside the lit area, other robots spot you 40% farther away, and the nearest patrol is called in.
* **Spark**: fires an electric dart that slows your car, with sparks crawling over the hull.
* **Lancer**: rocket strike on an area.
* **Sower**: mines your route, up to 8 mines at a time.
* **Mender**: welds damaged robots back together, so it’s the one to take out first.
* **Breacher**: rams you and blows up. If it misses, it drives back to its post.
* **Cinder**: flamethrower. Fire ignores armor, burns the crew and leaves burning patches on the ground.

Night is more dangerous: rovers see farther, Beacon joins in, and fire and sparks light up the ground. The video shows the same route twice, first at night, then by day.

Besides the rovers, a lot of work went into optimization: rendering is faster and memory load is lower. The HUD has also been completely redone: a bottom panel with the vehicle, health, water, fuel and hull, a minimap, a day/night dial, and queued notifications. The video already shows the new HUD.

What module would you add next?
